d: Outside view of the city of Thebes, and the field of the clays. In the middle, large fence with double entrance, intended for the fight of the two rival brothers, and on a magnificent stage for the judges of the duel.

In time for the people to take the two corpses elsewhere, they come out hurried and anxiously from the city gate, following their Donzelles, making their way among the crowd of the People, who on their arrival dispose respectful of the two sides of the scene Antigona, and Ismene.

Wide deserted countryside at the foot of bare mountains, with a view in the distance of a part of the city. The scene is in time at night, if not how much is illuminated by the flames of a burning fire, on which the corpse of Polynice burns.
